summary:
ASHE is an offline-first health monitoring and decision-support app that helps astronauts detect and act on health changes during long-duration missions, when real-time ground support is limited. It addresses four spaceflight hazards: radiation, isolation and confinement, altered gravity, and hostile closed environments.

ASHE combines wearable sensor readings, environmental data, and self-reports to track heart rate, blood pressure, blood oxygen, respiratory rate, sleep, stress, activity, and radiation exposure. It builds a personalized baseline for each astronaut and analyzes trends to catch early warning signs.

A three-level alert system (Green, Yellow, Red) tells astronauts what to do next. Data is stored securely onboard, and essential summaries sync with ground teams when communication is available.

Our prototype app demonstrates this baseline tracking and alert logic, with health indicators and thresholds grounded in NASA Human Research Program (HRP) research on spaceflight health risks.

ASHE aims to increase astronaut autonomy, enable timely medical intervention, and support safer exploration beyond Earth.
details:
What it does

ASHE is a health monitoring and decision-support app for astronauts on long-duration space missions. On these missions, astronauts carry much of the responsibility for noticing health changes in themselves, and real-time support from Earth is limited. ASHE helps them detect early warning signs and decide what to do next.

How it works

ASHE combines three sources of information: wearable sensor readings, environmental data, and astronaut self-reports. It tracks heart rate, blood pressure, blood oxygen, respiratory rate, sleep quality, stress, physical activity, and radiation exposure. The system first builds a personalized baseline for each astronaut. It then compares new data against that baseline and analyzes trends over time, so it can flag meaningful changes for that specific person instead of relying only on generic thresholds.

Results are shown through a three-level alert system:

- Green: indicators are within the astronaut's normal range.

- Yellow: a trend needs attention, and the astronaut is guided to adjust and monitor.

- Red: a serious change that calls for immediate action and contact with the ground medical team.

Hazards addressed

ASHE is designed around four major spaceflight hazards: space radiation, isolation and confinement, altered gravity, and hostile closed environments. Each hazard affects different health indicators, so the system monitors physical, environmental, and psychological signals together.

Offline-first design

ASHE is designed to work on board without a constant connection to Earth. Data is stored securely onboard, and essential health summaries are synchronized with ground teams whenever communication is available.

Benefits and impact

- Increases astronaut autonomy during missions far from Earth.

- Enables timely medical intervention by catching changes early.

- Turns complex health data into clear, actionable guidance.

- Supports safer human exploration beyond Earth.

What makes it creative

Instead of one-size-fits-all limits, ASHE personalizes monitoring for each astronaut. It also brings physical health, environmental conditions, and mental well-being into one simple Green/Yellow/Red view.

Research basis

The health indicators and alert logic are grounded in NASA Human Research Program (HRP) research on spaceflight health risks, and we reviewed NASA's life sciences resources listed in the NASA Data section.

Our prototype

Our prototype demonstrates the baseline tracking and alert logic described above.
